# Word Ladder (Bidirectional BFS)

Turn **cold** into **warm** one letter at a time, with every step a real word: cold, cord, word, worm, warm. It's a route-finding problem in disguise. Each word is a place, words one letter apart are joined, and breadth-first search finds the shortest ladder.

The idea worth learning: a breadth-first search's frontier grows fast with every step. Searching from **both ends** and stopping where they meet swaps one deep search for two shallow ones, which usually touch far fewer words.

How the cells run:

- **Clojure runs in your browser** with Scittle, so it starts at once, on the website too. In the full hub, the **⚙ Runtime Center** can switch Clojure to the JVM in the Linux VM; these cells run there too, just more slowly.
- **Clojure reads and shares `nb`.** The first cell shares its results with `nb`, and section 3 reads them back with `nb/get`.

> ✨ The code cells were written by an AI model from prompts, and each prompt is saved in its cell: press **✨** in a cell's header to see it.

Press **Run all**.

## 1. Climb the ladder

> In Clojure, find a word ladder from "cold" to "warm" through a dictionary of 70 four-letter words, changing one letter at a time. Write neighbors, which tries all 26 letters in each of the 4 places, then a one-way breadth-first search and a bidirectional one that always grows the smaller side, each recording the size of every frontier it expands. Print both ladders, how many words each search touched, and the frontier sizes, and publish nb.ladder: {ladder, oneway, bidi (the frontier sizes), onewayExpanded, bidiExpanded, words (the dictionary, sorted)}.

- **`neighbors`** is a `for` over every place and every letter, keeping only real words. That's the whole map: nothing lists the connections in advance.
- **`bfs`** grows a set of words one ring at a time. `parent` remembers where each word was reached from, so `path-of` can walk the ladder back.
- **`bidi`** keeps a frontier at each end and always grows the smaller one. `(some fa fb)` finds a word both sides have reached: the meeting point.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

(def words
  #{"cold" "cord" "card" "ward" "warm" "word" "worm" "wart" "want" "wand"
    "cool" "coal" "corn" "core" "care" "cart" "carp" "harp" "hard" "harm"
    "farm" "form" "fort" "sort" "sore" "bore" "bare" "bark" "dark" "dart"
    "mart" "mast" "most" "host" "hose" "nose" "note" "node" "code" "mode"
    "made" "mare" "more" "wore" "work" "tore" "torn" "turn" "burn" "born"
    "barn" "yarn" "earn" "ears" "eats" "oats" "oath" "bath" "bats" "rats"
    "raft" "rift" "gift" "girl" "gill" "will" "wall" "ball" "bald" "bold"})

(defn neighbors [w]
  (for [i (range 4)
        c "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
        :let [nw (str (subs w 0 i) c (subs w (inc i) 4))]
        :when (and (not= nw w) (contains? words nw))]
    nw))

;; --- one-way BFS, recording the frontier size at every level ----------
(defn bfs [start target]
  (loop [frontier #{start}
         parent {start nil}
         sizes []]
    (cond
      (contains? parent target)
      {:sizes sizes :parent parent :expanded (count parent)}

      (empty? frontier)
      {:sizes sizes :parent parent :expanded (count parent)}

      :else
      (let [pairs (for [w frontier, nw (neighbors w)
                        :when (not (contains? parent nw))] [nw w])
            parent' (reduce (fn [p [nw w]] (if (contains? p nw) p (assoc p nw w)))
                            parent pairs)
            frontier' (set (remove #(contains? parent %) (map first pairs)))]
        (recur frontier' parent' (conj sizes (count frontier)))))))

(defn path-of [parent w]
  (loop [w w, acc []]
    (if (nil? w) acc (recur (parent w) (cons w acc)))))

;; --- bidirectional: always expand the SMALLER frontier ----------------
(defn bidi [start target]
  (loop [fa #{start} pa {start nil}
         fb #{target} pb {target nil}
         sizes []]
    (let [meet (some fa fb)]
      (cond
        meet
        {:sizes sizes
         :expanded (+ (count pa) (count pb))
         :ladder (concat (path-of pa meet) (rest (reverse (path-of pb meet))))}

        (or (empty? fa) (empty? fb))
        {:sizes sizes :expanded (+ (count pa) (count pb)) :ladder nil}

        :else
        (let [[f p] (if (<= (count fa) (count fb)) [fa pa] [fb pb])
              pairs (for [w f, nw (neighbors w) :when (not (contains? p nw))] [nw w])
              p' (reduce (fn [m [nw w]] (if (contains? m nw) m (assoc m nw w))) p pairs)
              f' (set (remove #(contains? p %) (map first pairs)))]
          (if (<= (count fa) (count fb))
            (recur f' p' fb pb (conj sizes (count f)))
            (recur fa pa f' p' (conj sizes (count f)))))))))

(def one (bfs "cold" "warm"))
(def ladder (vec (path-of (:parent one) "warm")))
(def two (bidi "cold" "warm"))

(println "one-way ladder:" (str/join " -> " ladder))
(println "one-way explored" (:expanded one) "words, frontier sizes" (:sizes one))
(println "bidi ladder:   " (str/join " -> " (:ladder two)))
(println "bidi explored  " (:expanded two) "words, frontier sizes" (:sizes two))

(defn ja [xs] (str "[" (str/join "," xs) "]"))
(defn js [xs] (str "[" (str/join "," (map #(str "\"" % "\"") xs)) "]"))

(println (str "__NB_SET__ {\"key\":\"ladder\",\"value\":{"
              "\"ladder\":" (js ladder)
              ",\"oneway\":" (ja (:sizes one))
              ",\"bidi\":" (ja (:sizes two))
              ",\"onewayExpanded\":" (:expanded one)
              ",\"bidiExpanded\":" (:expanded two)
              ",\"words\":" (js (sort words)) "}}"))

## 3. Map the dictionary

> In Clojure, read the dictionary the first cell shared (nb.ladder's words) with nb/get, and map it out from "cold": search breadth-first and print the words at each distance, then the words that can't be reached at all, and the average number of one-letter neighbours a word has. If there's no dictionary yet, say to run the first cell.

The ladder is one route; this is the whole map around it. It's a separate program, so it gets the dictionary from `nb` rather than from the first cell's variables. That way it works on the JVM too.

- **`(nb/get :ladder)`** returns what the first cell shared, as Clojure data, and `{:keys [words]}` takes the dictionary out of it.
- **`group-by`** sorts the words into piles by distance, one pile per ring of the search.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

(if-let [{:keys [words]} (nb/get :ladder)]
  (let [dict (set words)
        neighbors (fn [w]
                    (for [i (range (count w))
                          c "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
                          :let [nw (str (subs w 0 i) c (subs w (inc i)))]
                          :when (and (not= nw w) (contains? dict nw))]
                      nw))
        ;; breadth-first from "cold": each ring is every word one step further out
        dist (loop [ring ["cold"], dist {"cold" 0}, d 0]
               (if (empty? ring)
                 dist
                 (let [next-ring (distinct (for [w ring, n (neighbors w) :when (not (contains? dist n))] n))]
                   (recur next-ring (into dist (map (fn [n] [n (inc d)]) next-ring)) (inc d)))))
        unreached (sort (remove #(contains? dist %) dict))
        links (reduce + (map #(count (neighbors %)) dict))]
    (println (count dist) "of" (count dict) "words can be reached from cold:")
    (doseq [[d pile] (sort (group-by val dist))]
      (println (format "  %d away: %s" d (str/join " " (sort (map key pile))))))
    (println (count unreached) "can't be reached at all:" (str/join " " unreached))
    (println (format "a word has %.2f one-letter neighbours on average" (double (/ links (count dict))))))
  (println "No dictionary yet: run the first Clojure cell."))

## What the run shows

- **Four steps: cold, cord, word, worm, warm.** Both searches find the same ladder. The one-way search touched 41 words and the bidirectional one 30, 27% fewer.
- **The frontiers tell why.** One way, they grow 1, 2, 5, 16; from both ends, never past 5. Each side only goes half as deep, and the last ring is always the biggest.
- **The map has islands.** 65 of the 70 words can be reached from cold, the farthest being bath and oath, 9 steps away. Coal and cool are joined only to each other, and gift, rift and raft only to each other, so no ladder reaches them.
- **A word has 3.51 neighbours on average.** That's few, so the saving here is modest. With a full dictionary, where short words have many more neighbours, the one-way frontier grows much faster, and meeting in the middle saves far more.

Each of these is a prompt. Press **✨** in a cell's header to change its prompt and generate it again, or **⚡ AI Generate New Cell** at the bottom to add a new one.

- **A longer climb.** Press ✨ on the first cell and change *"from cold to warm"* to *"from bold to nose"*. Do the two frontier lines move further apart?

- **Every shortest ladder.** New Clojure cell: *"Read nb.ladder's words with nb/get and print every shortest ladder from cold to warm, not just one."*
